title: Chemical Bonding II (Geometry) - Chemistry - Intermolecular Forces
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which elements must hydrogen be bonded to for Hydrogen Bonding to occur?
questions.explain: Hydrogen bonds form when hydrogen is covalently bonded to one of the three most electronegative elements: Nitrogen (N), Oxygen (O), or Fluorine (F). [Source: Chem LibreTexts](https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/General_Chemistry/Map%3A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)/11%3A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces/11.02%3A_Intermolecular_Forces)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which intermolecular force is present in all molecules, regardless of polarity?
questions.explain: London dispersion forces (also called induced dipole-induced dipole forces) exist between all atoms and molecules. [Source: Chem LibreTexts](https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/General_Chemistry/Map%3A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)/11%3A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces/11.02%3A_Intermolecular_Forces)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why does $n​$-pentane have a higher boiling point ($36.1^\circ C$) than its isomer neopentane ($9.5^\circ C$)?
options: $n​$-pentane has a larger surface area for contact, increasing London dispersion forces.
Neopentane has a higher molar mass.
questions.explain: The linear shape of n-pentane provides a greater surface area for intermolecular contact compared to the spherical shape of neopentane, resulting in stronger London dispersion forces. [Source: Chem LibreTexts](https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/General_Chemistry/Map%3A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)/11%3A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces/11.02%3A_Intermolecular_Forces)

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is expected to have the highest boiling point?
questions.explain: Acetone is a polar molecule with dipole-dipole interactions, which are stronger than the London dispersion forces found in the nonpolar alkanes listed (2-methylpropane, propane, methane).
